symptom: Daily briefs read as a dumb heuristic RSS digest; founder called the product worse than his Pipedream finance flow.
root_cause: CORRECTED after S1 (PS, 2026-06-14, verified vs live DB): the '0 AI calls' was a TELEMETRY GAP, not a dead AI. No route ever wrote pipeline_runs.ai_calls_made/ai_tokens_used (all 499 rows = 0) even though score (Gemini) and generate (Claude) DID fire — generate produced real claude-sonnet briefs (e.g., 05-17). What made briefs LOOK heuristic was a curate->generate CLOBBER: curate's upsert re-stamped generation_model='heuristic'/prompt_version on every 30-min tick, overwriting the Claude label generate had written (it left summary_html, producing the AI-HTML-with-'heuristic'-label contradiction). Compounded by the dispatcher stalling after 2026-06-13.
fix: S1 (done + verified): curate no longer clobbers generate's fields (updates curation fields only; new briefs insert with summary_html NULL); telemetry now records ai_calls_made/ai_tokens_used at the router for score+generate; fail-loud watchdog flags any run that did work but made 0 AI calls; ops metric GET /api/ops/ai-telemetry. Verified live: 06-14 score=1582 tok, generate=1830 tok, brief=claude-sonnet-4-6 and stays claude on curate re-run. Commits fce39ef (seam) + 3af7400 (telemetry).
golden_rule: An untracked metric is not evidence: ai_calls_made=0 meant 'no route wrote the column', not 'the AI never fired' — it fooled the live-DB forensics. Wire the telemetry FIRST, prove it records a known-true case, THEN trust its zero. A step reporting status='completed' still isn't proof it did its job. See lessons.md #104, #108, #111.

symptom: Briefs served irrelevant generic world news (e.g. Australian NDIS policy) to a US finance-focused user.
root_cause: user_preferences.topics, tracked_tickers, excluded_topics are all []. With no per-user relevance anchor, two high-volume generic feeds (BBC World, Guardian World) dominated the 13 finance/econ/AI feeds. The differentiator (personalization) was never populated, yet features were stacked on top of it.
fix: Seed and wire the per-user interest graph (topics + tracked_tickers) so relevance scoring has a real anchor; down-rank generic feeds for a focused user.
golden_rule: Prove the core differentiator end-to-end on one real user (measured) BEFORE building any peripheral feature. An empty load-bearing layer = a hollow moat. See lessons.md #106, wired-not-orphaned.md.

symptom: Every brief showed 'N stories . core' with no real categories; all 184 scored articles fell in diversity_category='core'.
root_cause: No strict resolution layer: the scoring/curation step never classifies into a real taxonomy mapped to DB rows; everything defaults to one 'core' bucket. AI category/entity outputs are not resolved to existing DB UUIDs.
fix: Add a strict resolution layer: the model may only output category/entity IDs that exist in the DB; on a miss, flag-for-review (do not blind-insert) and retry.
golden_rule: AI hallucinates strings; databases require relations. Resolve every AI-extracted category/entity to an existing DB UUID before insert; an invented value fails the run. See lessons.md #105, VIBE Rule 24.

symptom: On the brief page Save flips to 'Saved' but there is nowhere to find saved items; Dismiss flips but the article stays; 'Took action' flips but nothing happens.
root_cause: article_outcomes rows are written (saved/dismissed/action_taken) but saved_items=0 (Save has no destination surface), the list is not re-filtered on dismiss, and action_taken has no downstream consumer. Outcome buttons write data with no visible effect.
fix: Wire a saved-items destination page; remove dismissed items from the view; give 'action' a real downstream (draft/act). No dead UI: every button works or is removed.
golden_rule: A button that writes a row but produces no visible effect is dead UI and destroys trust. Wire it to a destination/consumer or remove it. See VIBE Rule 51.

symptom: Per-article summaries cut off mid-sentence ('...who believ'); scored_articles.one_line_summary is NULL on every row.
root_cause: The scoring step never populates one_line_summary, so the surface falls back to a truncated raw snippet. Combined with ERR-019 (AI generation never ran) the brief shows truncated, un-synthesized text.
fix: Populate a substring-validated one_line_summary during scoring/generation; render full synthesized text, not a truncated raw snippet.
golden_rule: Never render a truncated raw snippet as if it were a summary. Produce (and validate) the digest field the UI reads.

symptom: The same article ('States tell Albanese government...NDIS') was served in BOTH the 06-10 and 06-11 briefs.
root_cause: Ingest dedups within a fetch (content_hash) but there is no cross-brief dedup: an article already delivered in a prior brief can be selected again. The 'second time' scenario was not handled at the curation layer.
fix: Track already-delivered article_ids per user and exclude them from subsequent curation (or down-weight), so a story is not re-served across briefs.
golden_rule: Design the second-time scenario for every user-facing surface, not just first use. Within-batch dedup is not cross-time dedup.

symptom: No brief generated after 2026-06-13; sources.last_fetched_at is NULL on all 15 sources though 193 raw_articles exist.
root_cause: The pg_cron dispatcher effectively stalled (~36h gap) with no alert; ingest writes raw_articles but never updates sources.last_fetched_at, so source health reports 'healthy' while stale (a health lie). No self-audit watched the pipeline telemetry.
fix: Add an ops/self-audit check on pipeline_runs (alert if a step makes 0 AI calls for N hours, delivery fails, or a brief has <N items); update sources.last_fetched_at on every fetch.
golden_rule: Instrument the pipeline to flag its own silence. A stalled cron + a 'healthy' source lie are invisible without a telemetry watchdog.

symptom: Every route threw ChunkLoadError at runtime on Cloudflare Workers; had to force a webpack build in open-next config.
root_cause: Next.js (Turbopack server chunks) + OpenNext on the Cloudflare Workers workerd runtime is a poor fit for heavy Node/AI-SDK server code; Workers' CPU/memory limits and chunk loading break the AI pipeline. The app deviated from the originally-intended Vercel target.
fix: Move the Next.js app off Cloudflare Workers; host on a full Node runtime (Railway chosen) with Supabase as the host-independent brain (pg_cron + pgvector). Keep portability so the host stays swappable.
golden_rule: Host heavy Node/AI server code on a full Node runtime, not an edge isolate; keep the brain (DB/vectors/cron) on a host-independent service so the host stays a swappable presentation layer.

symptom: Even after S1 wired telemetry, every article scored relevance/composite 0.50 and category 'uncategorized' — scoring was garbage while telemetry showed the AI 'fired' (ai_calls_made=1).
root_cause: gemini-2.5-flash is a THINKING model; its reasoning tokens consumed the entire output budget, so it returned empty text -> JSON.parse threw 'Unexpected end of JSON input' -> scorer.ts catch swallowed it into per-batch default 5/5/5 scores. The call succeeded (tokens billed, ai_calls_made=1) but produced no usable JSON, so scoring silently defaulted. Fourth silent-fallback in the same family as the curate clobber (ERR-019) and the hardcoded category (ERR-021).
fix: Set thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget:0 for the triage/score model + multi-part text extraction + 4096-token output headroom. Cost rose $0.0006 -> $0.0039 = real output. Verified live: score now 7 calls / 29913 tokens with real per-article scores + 14 real categories (was 1 call / 1582 tokens of empty output).
golden_rule: When using a 'thinking' model for structured JSON extraction, disable thinking (thinkingBudget:0) or reserve explicit output headroom — reasoning tokens can starve the output and return empty JSON. And a catch that swallows a parse error into default values hides a broken AI call behind a 'healthy' run: surface it, never default silently.

status: FIXED in code 2026-07-01 — parse-time id validation + uuid-shape guard landed with the ERR-029 fail-loud bundle (commit 654113d; mangledIdsDropped telemetry). Live-cron proof pending the E6 host cutover (the stale Cloudflare dispatcher still runs the pre-fix bundle).
symptom: After S3.1 hardening, the unattended score step fails ~every tick: ~10 consecutive ticks (14:40–14:51 UTC, 06-15) failed with 'scored_articles batch upsert failed: invalid input syntax for type uuid: "284354a-702a-43ac-aabb-a4a713760d49"'. 139 raw_articles stuck in pipeline_status='fetched', not advancing; only rounds where the AI happened to return all-clean ids completed (100 in / 100 scored).
root_cause: The Gemini scorer NON-DETERMINISTICALLY echoes a CORRUPTED copy of an input article id (drops one hex char: real id 2843554a-702a-43ac-aabb-a4a713760d49 -> emitted 284354a-...; 3f36369d-... -> 3f363636d-...). Proven decisively: the malformed string matches a real raw_articles.id off by one dropped char, so it is a mangled ARTICLE id, not a ticker/entity id. S3.1's guard validArticleIds.has(score.articleId) in score/route.ts was supposed to drop it, but on the live Cloudflare host the bad id still reaches the SINGLE all-or-nothing batch upsert — and one invalid uuid rejects the whole batch -> run throws -> status='failed' -> no articles advance -> same batch re-fetched next tick -> failure loop. Two contributing causes: (1) AI structured-output corruption (same family as ERR-027); (2) brittleness — the guard must be perfect AND the upsert is all-or-nothing. Likely the live Cloudflare bundle predates/omits the filter (stale-deploy, ERR-026 class; forgeminds_base_url still = forgeminds.vctrbbnv.workers.dev, Railway cutover not done).
fix: Layer 1 DONE 2026-07-01 (commit 654113d, folded into the ERR-029 fail-loud bundle): parse-time validation in scorer.ts drops any AI-returned item whose id is not in the input batch or not UUID-shaped (mangledIdsDropped counter written to pipeline_runs.metadata) BEFORE the row builder; the route's validArticleIds filter retained as layer 2. Per-row upsert isolation deliberately NOT built — moot unless mangled_ids_dropped>0 telemetry ever proves recurrence. Layer 3 (host cutover so the live dispatcher runs the fixed bundle) superseded: Vercel replaces Railway (DECISIONS 2026-07-03), scheduled at E6 — that is where the live-cron proof of this fix lands.
golden_rule: An AI can corrupt even an identifier you handed it — never trust an LLM to echo ids verbatim. Validate every AI-returned id against the known input set at parse time and drop non-matches there; never let one bad row fail an all-or-nothing batch (pre-validate/coerce or isolate). And a point-in-time local 'it scored 92' proof can hide a host that fails every unattended tick — verify the live telemetry, not the handoff. See lessons.md #105, #108, #111; ERR-021, ERR-027.

status: FIXED in code 2026-07-01 (fail-loud guard); live activation pending founder host-secret update + deploy. ANNOTATION 2026-07-09: E1's relevance gate passed LOCALLY (commits 1123f8b + a8f31d2 — real Claude calls against the dev DB, finance-first brief with zero generic-news leak; the JSON-fence-strip parse fix in 1123f8b is what restored real per-article scoring). STAYS OPEN until the live-cron proof at E6 — the stale Cloudflare dispatcher still runs the pre-fix bundle and writes legacy diversity_category='core' rows into dev every ~30 min (known, parked until the E6 host cutover).
symptom: For ~16 days (2026-06-15 to 07-01) every score and generate run reported status='completed' while making 0 AI calls (live DB: 91/91 runs 'completed' per step in 72h, ai_calls_made=0 on all). The pipeline shipped heuristic default-scored briefs the whole time and no gate fired. Discovered only by a live-DB verification sweep - which also showed the 16-day-old handoff doc was wrong (ERR-028's failure loop was NOT reproducing).
root_cause: Compound: (1) the live Cloudflare host's Gemini/Anthropic secrets were dead (stale, then the founder's 07-01 key rotation), so every AI call threw; (2) scorer.ts's batch catch swallowed each failure into fabricated default 5/5/5 scores - the exact anti-pattern ERR-027's golden rule named, sitting in the OTHER catch of the same file; (3) the S1 AI-zero-call watchdog was console.error ONLY - it logged into the void and the run still wrote status='completed'; (4) score/route.ts advanced pipeline_status='scored' for ALL fetched articles regardless of scoring success, burying the evidence. Net effect: a dead API key produced permanently-green telemetry. Inverse twin of ERR-019 (there the AI fired but telemetry said it didn't; here telemetry said 'completed' while the AI never fired).
fix: Fail-loud guard (2026-07-01): scorer.ts no longer emits default scores on batch failure (failed batches contribute nothing; their articles stay 'fetched' and retry, bounded by score_lookback_minutes) + parse-time validation drops any AI-returned item whose id is not in the input batch or not UUID-shaped (mangledIdsDropped counter = ERR-028 layer-1 defense landed as part of this). score/route.ts throws AI_ZERO_CALL (status='failed') when articles>0 and aiCallsMade=0, advances pipeline_status ONLY for rows actually persisted, and records mangled_ids_dropped/batches_failed/articles_unscored in run metadata. generate/route.ts throws AI_ZERO_CALL when aiAttempts>0 and aiCallsMade=0 (briefs keep summary_html NULL and re-heal next tick, so failing loses nothing). tsc 0 errors, lint 0 errors. ACTIVATION: founder must (a) put the NEW Gemini/Anthropic keys into the host secrets and (b) deploy this bundle - until then the OLD silent code is what runs live.
golden_rule: A console.error watchdog is not a gate - a run that had real work and made 0 AI calls must FAIL, not warn (lessons #104/#111: status='completed' is not evidence the job happened). Never persist fabricated fallback output on AI failure; leave the work undone and retryable so the failure stays visible and self-heals. Advance pipeline state only for items that actually succeeded - a blanket status update buries partial failures. And re-verify a 2-week-old handoff against live telemetry before building the fix it prescribes: the bug it names may be gone and a worse one hiding (lesson #108).
